entities.name: Coinbase National Trust Company

regulatory_status.cas_status: Approved 2026-04-02; no Consummated/Effective date shown in retrieved CAS detail
regulatory_status.operational_status: OCC charter commencement not established from the retrieved CAS record

scope: fiduciary digital-asset custody primarily for institutional clients
accept, hold and transfer custodied fiat and digital assets only within customer custodial accounts
fiat custody balances held in for-benefit-of accounts at third-party banks
facilitate custody clients' access to affiliate staking, Prime Trading and Prime Financing as a finder; the bank itself does not provide those underlying affiliate services

entities.additional_liquidity_requirement: 180 days of operating expenses in eligible liquid assets; cannot double-count assets used for the Tier 1 liquid-asset condition.
entities.evidence_limit: Initial conditional approval conditions may be amended in a final approval; the retrieved CAS record has no effective date.

commonalities: All three are national trust-company charters, not ordinary full-service commercial-bank charters.
All three are non-insured depository institutions under the described approval conditions.
All three require OCC pre-opening compliance and supervisory review.
All three initial approval letters say the institution will apply for stock in a Federal Reserve Bank; this is not proof of a Federal Reserve master account or direct Fedwire access.
strategic_differences: Ripple and Circle proposed stablecoin-reserve management and collateral-trustee models, with issuance remaining in separate New York limited-purpose trust entities.

Coinbase proposed a large institutional custody and customer-transaction model, with related access to affiliate staking, Prime Trading and Prime Financing; fiat custody uses third-party-bank FBO accounts.

Coinbase's initial minimum Tier 1 capital requirement is $60m, versus $11.7m for Ripple and $6.05m for Circle. These are initial regulatory minimums, not actual paid-in capital, total corporate capital or a direct measure of company strength.
comparison.xrp_scope: None of the three retrieved OCC decision letters identifies XRP as a required reserve asset or as a specific charter-purpose asset. Ripple's letter centers on RLUSD; Circle's on USDC; Coinbase's on institutional digital-asset custody generally. XRP custody eligibility or actual usage requires separate evidence.
comparison.federal_reserve_access: The Fed's master-account database is a separate source, current as of 2026-08-31. The OCC letters' requirement to apply for Federal Reserve Bank stock is not equivalent to a master account. No exact row for Ripple, Circle or Coinbase was verified in this run.

confirmed_fact: OCC letters define the initial proposed scope and capital conditions.
OCC CAS records Circle and Ripple as Consummated/Effective and Coinbase as Approved without a displayed effective date in the retrieved record.
inference: The charters reflect distinct but overlapping competition for regulated custody, stablecoin reserve administration and institutional transaction infrastructure.
speculation: Different minimum capital requirements may reflect differences in the proposed operating scope, scale, risk or OCC assessment; the documents do not establish the reason for the differences.
unknown: Final-condition amendments after initial conditional approvals
